title: Peckhamist Optical Tradition, c. 1270–1665: A List of Manuscript and Printed Texts
description:
The dataset contains a list of around 50 medieval and Renaissance optical texts belonging to the Peckhamist tradition. It lists all manuscript and printed texts discovered and identified to date that derive from the medieval optical treatise Perspectiva communis by John Peckham and originated between the 1270s and 1665. Only textual units are listed, not specific copies, whether manuscript or printed. (Some of these textual units, however, exists in a single copy, such as specific sets of marginal annotations and commentaries in a manuscript or a printed copy.) Similarly, only texts that differ somewhat from the original Peckham’s treatise are listed, such as its redactions, compilations based on it and commentaries on it (whether in the form of textual expositiones, quaestiones, or significant sets of marginal notes and comments). Together, these textual units constitute the "Peckhamist" tradition in late medieval and Renaissance optics, revealing a pan-European textual corpus, spanning England, France, Italy, Spain and Central Europe from the late 13th to the early 17th century.
 
The bibliographic data were collected and compiled as a by-product of the broader research behind the preparation of a new catalogue of medieval and Renaissance optical manuscripts within the project "The Age of Peckham: The Role of John Peckham's Perspectiva communis in the Dissemination and Development of Optical Knowledge, 1279–1542" funded by the Czech Science Foundation (GAČR, grant no. 24-12752S).
